doc.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03

title: Albert's mother and siblings
summary: His mother Georgiana was a housewife; the order of his siblings and Leo's much later birth.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Right. And did you hear people walking along playing the harmonica much around New Orleans?
Harmonica was not a big instrument. I don't think so. Did your mother work?
No, my mother was a housewife. And her name? Georgiana. Georgiana.
But she had enough to do, folks. Yes, she did.
Imagine. There's a good deal of difference in the ages of the children, because Dutch is much younger than you.

Well, you see, you're counting Dutch, but what about the ones before Dutch? You had my sister, then a brother Stanley, then me, and my brother Maurice, then Dutch, then Leo. I mean, she's the youngest, Dutch?
So he's much younger. Yeah. That's right. You told me his, your mother was old when he was. He was 48 when he was born. 48.
The last button on the air was good.
And how old is Leo now?
Well, he's about my age, roughly.
